experiments.scope: Selected three-engine HTTP-400 diagnostic on the same current image, one attempt per target/engine. Not a full API or repeated-round result.

conclusion: The initial driver portfolio and retained-homepage warm-up added no exclusive coverage. All three engines timed out before the Roblox destination committed. The later newly-hosted lululemon HTTP-400 probe did find a Firefox marker match where both Chromium drivers returned 400, motivating a separately measured API eligibility repair. The Canada Goose metadata-only marker remains a failure; no default engine, blanket warm-up or Roblox deadline-splitting change was justified.
limits: The consent/transport probe returned four of eight planned observations before Firefox memory.events:max reached 196. OOM and OOM-kill counters remained zero. The guard stopped the experiment and all created containers were removed; incomplete cases are not inferred as observed failures.
One selected observation per engine/target or warm-up policy is not stable availability or proof that a technique can never work.
Driver comparisons use the same image and egress, while browser protocol implementations differ. WAF labels are publisher categories, not proof of an active commercial rule.

Warm-up adds a homepage request and three-second delay, uses a retained origin-fenced tab and disables automatic consent-library actions for that retained tab. It is not a cookie-only experiment. All six retained sessions were explicitly removed.
A 30-second pre-commit timeout does not prove a permanent outage or identify whether network, route, server or access policy is responsible.
Raw session capabilities stay in private local artifacts; this receipt contains no session tokens or cookie values.
